es.summary: Reducción transitoria del flujo sanguíneo coronario que provoca daño isquémico al miocardio y dolor torácico típico.
key_points: Causada por aterosclerosis que estrecha la arteria coronaria ≥50 %.
Dolor torácico opresivo que empeora con el esfuerzo y mejora con reposo o nitroglicerina.
Diagnóstico basado en ECG, marcadores de daño miocárdico y pruebas de imagen.
Tratamiento inmediato: aspirina, oxígeno, nitroglicerina y, según gravedad, anticoagulación o reperfusión.

pathophysiology: Placa aterosclerótica reduce el diámetro luminal de la arteria coronaria.
Disminución del flujo coronario → hipoxia miocárdica.
Desbalance entre demanda y suministro de oxígeno genera dolor y disfunción contractil.
Si la isquemia persiste, se produce necrosis (infarto).
risk_factors: Edad avanzada y antecedentes familiares de enfermedad coronaria.
signs_symptoms: Dolor torácico opresivo, a menudo irradiado a brazo izquierdo, mandíbula o espalda.
Disnea de inicio súbito o con el esfuerzo.
Fatiga y sensación de presión en el pecho.
diagnostics: ECG: depresión o elevación del ST, ondas T invertidas.
Troponina I o T >0.04 ng/mL y CK‑MB elevadas.
Prueba de esfuerzo o angiografía coronaria para confirmar estenosis ≥50 %.
Perfil lipídico y glucemia en ayunas para identificar factores de riesgo.
treatment: Nitroglicerina sublingual 0.4 mg para aliviar dolor.
Heparina de bajo peso molecular o unfractionated para anticoagulación.
Terapia de reperfusión (PCI o trombolíticos como alteplasa) según indicación.
Betabloqueadores y estatinas en fase subaguda.
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor antes, durante y después del esfuerzo (escala 0‑10).
Monitorear signos vitales y ECG continuo.
Mantener vía IV de acceso rápido y administrar medicamentos según prescripción.
Posicionar al paciente en semi‑Fowler para reducir la demanda cardíaca.
Administrar oxígeno y nitroglicerina según protocolo.
Registrar respuesta a la terapia y notificar cambios al médico.
patient_teaching: Reconocer y reportar dolor torácico o disnea inmediata.
Tomar aspirina y otros fármacos según indicación, sin omitir dosis.
Adoptar hábitos saludables: dieta baja en grasas, ejercicio regular y abandono del tabaco.
Controlar presión arterial, glucemia y lípidos en controles periódicos.
Programar citas de seguimiento y pruebas de estrés según indicación.

outcomes: Nivel de tolerancia a la actividad: paciente caminará 100 m sin dolor en 7 días.
Frecuencia cardíaca permanecerá entre 60‑100 lpm durante actividad leve.

interventions.action: Evaluar dolor torácico y frecuencia cardíaca antes de iniciar cualquier actividad.
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar intolerancia y prevenir isquemia adicional.

interventions.action: Administrar nitroglicerina sublingual 5 min antes de actividad programada si está prescrita.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la demanda de oxígeno al vasodilatación coronaria.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente técnicas de pacing (descansos breves cada 5 min).
interventions.rationale: Distribuye la carga de trabajo y evita sobrecarga cardíaca.

interventions.action: Monitorear saturación de oxígeno y presión arterial durante la actividad.
interventions.rationale: Detecta deterioro hemodinámico temprano.

interventions.action: Documentar nivel de dolor y signos de fatiga después de la actividad.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la evaluación de la efectividad del plan de cuidados.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de disminución de la perfusión tisular cardíaca
outcomes: Sin episodios de dolor torácico durante 48 h de observación.
Presión arterial mantenida > 90/60 mmHg y SaO₂ > 94 %.

interventions.action: Monitorear ECG continuo y reportar cualquier cambio de ST o arritmia.
interventions.rationale: Detecta precozmente disminución de perfusión miocárdica.

interventions.action: Administrar aspirina según orden y registrar respuesta.
interventions.rationale: Previene formación de nuevos trombos que comprometan el flujo.

interventions.action: Mantener al paciente en posición semi‑Fowler (30‑45°).
interventions.rationale: Reduce la presión intratorácica y mejora el retorno venoso.

interventions.action: Proveer oxígeno suplementario para mantener SaO₂ > 94 %.
interventions.rationale: Aumenta la disponibilidad de oxígeno para el miocardio isquémico.

interventions.action: Evaluar y registrar signos de insuficiencia cardíaca (edema, disnea ortopédica).
interventions.rationale: Identifica complicaciones tempranas de perfusión insuficiente.

en.summary: Transient reduction of coronary blood flow that causes ischemic damage to the myocardium and typical chest pain.
key_points: Caused by atherosclerosis that narrows the coronary artery ≥50 %.
Oppressive chest pain that worsens with exertion and improves with rest or nitroglycerin.
Diagnosis based on ECG, myocardial injury markers, and imaging tests.
Immediate treatment: aspirin, oxygen, nitroglycerin and, depending on severity, anticoagulation or reperfusion.

pathophysiology: Atherosclerotic plaque reduces the luminal diameter of the coronary artery.
Imbalance between oxygen demand and supply generates pain and contractile dysfunction.
risk_factors: Advanced age and family history of coronary disease.
signs_symptoms: Oppressive chest pain, often radiating to the left arm, jaw, or back.
Sudden onset dyspnea or with exertion.
Fatigue and a sense of pressure in the chest.
diagnostics: ECG: ST depression or elevation, inverted T waves.
Troponin I or T >0.04 ng/mL and elevated CK‑MB.
Exercise test or coronary angiography to confirm stenosis ≥50 %.
Lipid profile and fasting glucose to identify risk factors.
treatment: Sublingual nitroglycerin 0.4 mg to relieve pain.
Low‑molecular‑weight heparin or unfractionated heparin for anticoagulation.
Reperfusion therapy (PCI or thrombolytics such as alteplase) as indicated.
Beta‑blockers and statins in the subacute phase.
nursing_care: Assess pain before, during, and after exertion (0‑10 scale).
Monitor vital signs and continuous ECG.
Maintain a rapid‑access IV line and administer medications per prescription.
Position patient in semi‑Fowler to reduce cardiac demand.
Administer oxygen and nitroglycerin per protocol.
Document response to therapy and notify physician of changes.
patient_teaching: Recognize and report chest pain or immediate dyspnea.
Take aspirin and other medications as prescribed, do not skip doses.
Adopt healthy habits: low‑fat diet, regular exercise, and smoking cessation.
Monitor blood pressure, glucose, and lipids during routine checkups.
Schedule follow‑up appointments and stress tests as indicated.

outcomes: Activity tolerance level: patient will walk 100 m without pain in 7 days.
Heart rate will remain between 60‑100 bpm during light activity.

interventions.action: Assess chest pain and heart rate before initiating any activity.
interventions.rationale: Allows identification of intolerance and prevents additional ischemia.

interventions.action: Administer sublingual nitroglycerin 5 min before scheduled activity if prescribed.
interventions.rationale: Reduces oxygen demand by coronary vasodilation.

interventions.action: Teach patient pacing techniques (brief rests every 5 min).
interventions.rationale: Distributes workload and avoids cardiac overload.

interventions.action: Monitor oxygen saturation and blood pressure during activity.
interventions.rationale: Detects early hemodynamic deterioration.

interventions.action: Document pain level and fatigue signs after activity.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates evaluation of care plan effectiveness.

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for decreased cardiac tissue perfusion
outcomes: No chest pain episodes during 48 h observation.
Blood pressure maintained > 90/60 mmHg and SaO₂ > 94 %.

interventions.action: Monitor continuous ECG and report any ST changes or arrhythmia.
interventions.rationale: Early detection of myocardial perfusion decrease.

interventions.action: Administer aspirin as ordered and record response.
interventions.rationale: Prevents formation of new thrombi that compromise flow.

interventions.action: Maintain patient in semi‑Fowler position (30‑45°).
interventions.rationale: Reduces intrathoracic pressure and improves venous return.

interventions.action: Provide supplemental oxygen to maintain SaO₂ > 94 %.
interventions.rationale: Increases oxygen availability for ischemic myocardium.

interventions.action: Assess and record signs of heart failure (edema, orthopnea).
interventions.rationale: Identifies early complications of insufficient perfusion.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Cardiac Emergency Drugs

summary.0.quote: Under the first condition of physical duress, called ischemia , the coronary artery becomes constricted to the point where blood flow is temporarily stopped but resumes with medication or rest.

key_points.0.quote: Obstructive CAD is when a large coronary artery is narrowed by 50% or more, significantly reducing blood flow.

key_points.3.quote: Four classifications of drugs may be used in emergency situations for AMI and unstable angina: aspirin, oxygen, nitroglycerin, and, occasionally, morphine.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: CAD develops slowly over time when plaque builds up inside your coronary arteries.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: If the same conditions occur, but blood flow to the myocardium is cut off completely, the cells die, called infarction .

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: Have a family history of heart disease, especially in a parent or sibling who had it before age 50 Are getting older, especially men, who tend to develop CAD earlier in life than women

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Classic symptoms include chest pain; pain radiating to the jaw, arms, neck, back, or stomach; shortness of breath; lightheadedness; and excessive sweating, also known as diaphoresis .

sections.diagnostics.0.quote: An EKG may demonstrate abnormalities with the T waves, in which the T waves will be flipped or the ST segment will be depressed ( Figure 12.23 ).

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: Order blood tests, including checking your cholesterol and blood glucose

sections.treatment.0.quote: For acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina: 325 mg orally (chewed) once.

sections.treatment.2.quote: Supplemental oxygen may be used if the client’s oxygen saturation is less than 94% on room air.

sections.complications.0.quote: An umbrella term, acute coronary syndrome (ACS) includes the following: non-ST-elevated myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), ST-elevated myocardial infarction (STEMI), and unstable angina ( Figure 12.24 ).

sections.complications.2.quote: If the patient has a depressed EF (less than 40%), ACE inhibitor s/ARBs will be initiated to reduce the risk of congestive heart failure.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Place the client on continuous cardiac monitoring.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: They notice chest pain; dyspnea; or numbness, tingling, or burning in their extremities.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Education is directed at dietary adjustments (low saturated fat, low cholesterol, monitor processed foods), smoking cessation, and limiting/omitting alcohol.
